sources.claim: Cloud Run run.googleapis.com/request_count is a DELTA INT64 count (unit 1) on cloud_run_revision with response_code and response_code_class labels; it counts requests reaching the revision and excludes requests that do not reach container instances; it is sampled every 60 seconds and data is not visible for up to 120 seconds after sampling. The page does not list the class values, so the fixture's '5xx' value is an authored console observation and is not graded.
The cloud_run_revision monitored resource carries project_id, service_name, revision_name, location and configuration_name labels, so request_count can be selected and grouped per revision.

Cloud Monitoring PromQL replaces the first '/' of a metric name with ':' and other special characters with '_', selects the resource type with the monitored_resource label, and filters resource labels directly. The run_googleapis_com:request_count name is derived from that rule, not quoted from the page; the page does not describe how increase() treats DELTA metrics, so the case grades the selectors and grouping, not function semantics.

A request-based goodTotalRatio SLI specifies exactly two of good, bad and total DELTA or CUMULATIVE INT64/DOUBLE series and assumes good + bad = total; the SLI is good_service / total_service over the queried interval; rollingPeriod is a whole number of days up to 30. The page does not state SLO behavior when series are absent.

Charts can show gaps when data is written very infrequently, because sampling may find no data. The page does not say whether a gap is displayed as zero, so the fixture states the absent buckets explicitly instead of relying on chart rendering.
When time-series data stops arriving or is delayed, Monitoring classifies it as missing; any replacement value used for alert evaluation is a configured choice, not an observed measurement.

a.conclusion: The panel's query matches every fx-rate-api revision and groups only by service_name, so its 97.0% is the service-wide ratio, not 5.6.0's. Grouped by revision_name with complete per-minute samples, the 5xx are on fx-rate-api-00030-wup (96.68% non-5xx, rising from the 09:22 minute before 5.6.0 was deployed), while fx-rate-api-00031-kez is at 99.94%. A 5.6.0 regression and a rollback to 00030-wup are unsupported; why 00030-wup returns 5xx is unknown.

Sasha keeps the traffic decision; moving all traffic to 00030-wup is not supported by this evidence, and any traffic shift toward 00031-kez is Sasha's decision under approval, not a diagnosed fix. Rory reports the bounded finding on the existing TLC.

Its 97.0% is 3 class-5xx responses out of 100 requests counted in 21 of 36 minutes; the other 15 minutes have no point for any response class.
